title: The College Report
instructions: Check your answers in the boxes.
reference: The College Student Report 2001. From the Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching and Pew Forum on Undergraduate Education (2002).

sections.prompt: During the current school year, about how often have you done each of the following?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Asked questions in class or contributed to class discussions

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Made a class presentation

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Prepared two or more drafts of a paper or assignment before turning it in

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Worked on a paper or project that required integrating ideas or information from various sources

questions.label: e.
questions.text: Came to class without completing readings or assignments

questions.label: f.
questions.text: Worked with other students on projects during class

questions.label: g.
questions.text: Worked with classmates outside of class to prepare class assignments

questions.label: h.
questions.text: Tutored or taught other students (paid or voluntary)

questions.label: i.
questions.text: Participated in a community-based project as part of a regular course

questions.label: j.
questions.text: Used an electronic medium (list-serv, chat group, Internet, etc.) to discuss or complete an assignment

questions.label: k.
questions.text: Used e-mail to communicate with an instructor

questions.label: l.
questions.text: Discussed grades or assignments with an instructor

questions.label: m
questions.text: Talked about career plans with a faculty member or advisor

questions.label: n.
questions.text: Discussed ideas from your reading or classes with faculty members outside of class

questions.label: o.
questions.text: Received prompt feedback from faculty on your academic performance (written or oral)

questions.label: p.
questions.text: Worked harder than you thought you could to meet an instructor's standards or expectations Worked with faculty members on activities other than coursework (committees, orientation, student life activities, etc.)

questions.label: q.
questions.text: Discussed ideas from your readings or classes with others outside of class (students, family members, coworkers, etc.

questions.label: r.
questions.text: Had serious conversations with students of a different race or ethnicity than your own

questions.label: s.
questions.text: Had serious conversations with students who differ from you in terms of their religious beliefs, political opinions, or personal values

sections.prompt: During the current academic year, to what extent has your coursework emphasized the following mental activities?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Memorizing facts, ideas, or methods from your courses and readings so you can repeat them in pretty much the same form

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Analyzing the basic elements of an idea, experience, or theory such as examining a particular case or situation in depth and considering its components

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Synthesizing and organizing ideas, information, or experiences into new, more complex interpretations and relationships

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Making judgments about the value of information, arguments, or methods such as examining how others gathered and interpreted data and assessing the soundness of their conclusions

questions.label: e.
questions.text: Applying theories or concepts to practical problems or in new situations

sections.prompt: During the current academic year, about how much reading and writing have you done?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Number of assigned textbooks, books, or book-length packs of course readings

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Number of books read on your own (not assigned) for personal enjoyment or academic enrichment

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Number of written papers or reports of 20 pages or more

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Number of written papers or reports between 5 and 19 pages

questions.label: e.
questions.text: Number of written papers or reports of fewer than 5 pages

sections.prompt: Mark the box that best represents the extent to which your examinations during the current school year have challenged you to do your best work.

questions.text: Mark the box that best represents the extent to which your examinations during the current school year have challenged you to do your best work.

sections.prompt: Which of the following have you done or you plan to do before you graduate from your institution?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Practicum, internship, field experience, co-op experience, or clinical assignment

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Community service or volunteer work

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Work on a research project with a faculty member outside of course or program requirements

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Foreign language coursework

questions.label: e.
questions.text: Study abroad

questions.label: f.
questions.text: Independent study or self-designed major

questions.label: g.
questions.text: Culminating senior experience (comprehensive exam, capstone course, thesis, project, etc.)

sections.prompt: About how many hours do you spend in a typical 7-day week doing each of the following?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Preparing for class (studying, reading, writing, rehearsing, and other activities related to your academic program)

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Participating in co-curricular activities (organizations, campus publications, student government, social fraternity or sorority, intercollegiate or intramural sports, etc.)

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Relaxing and socializing (watching TV, partying, exercising, playing computer and other games, etc.)

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Providing care for dependents living with you (parents, children, spouse, etc.)

sections.prompt: To what extent has your institution experience contributed to your knowledge, skills, and personal development in the following areas?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Acquiring a broad general education

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Acquiring job or work-related knowledge and skills

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Writing clearly and effectively

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Speaking clearly and effectively

questions.label: e.
questions.text: Thinking critically and analytically

questions.label: f.
questions.text: Analyzing quantitative problems

questions.label: g.
questions.text: Using computing and information technology

questions.label: h.
questions.text: Working effectively with others

questions.label: i.
questions.text: Voting in local, state, or national elections

questions.label: j.
questions.text: Learning effectively on your own

questions.label: k.
questions.text: Understanding yourself

questions.label: m
questions.text: Understanding people of other racial and ethnic backgrounds

questions.label: n.
questions.text: Developing a personal code of values and ethics

questions.label: o.
questions.text: Contributing to the welfare of your community

sections.prompt: To what extent does your institution emphasize each of the following?

questions.label: a.
questions.text: Spending significant amounts of time studying and on academic work

questions.label: b.
questions.text: Providing the support you need to help you succeed academicall

questions.label: c.
questions.text: Encouraging contact among students from different economic, social, and racial or ethnic backgrounds

questions.label: d.
questions.text: Helping you cope with your non-academic responsibilities (work, family, etc.)

questions.label: e.
questions.text: Providing the support you need to thrive socially

sections.prompt: How would you evaluate your entire educational experience at this institution?

questions.text: How would you evaluate your entire educational experience at this institution?

sections.note: The source provides blank response space, without a choice scale. Written response is optional.
